When Apple unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12, two features immediately caught my eye: the new Siri Recap feature and the significantly upgraded heart rate monitor. While these two features were part of the reason I picked up the new-generation Apple Watch, I discovered there were even more surprises in store.

Battery and Charging

Although Apple's website doesn't list any additional battery life improvements for the Apple Watch Series 12 compared to the Series 11, the battery does feel more durable. As I mentioned earlier, before using the Apple Watch Series 12, I had been a WHOOP user; although I always wore my Apple Watch, I never used it to track my sleep.

After the presentation ended, I decided to give the Apple Watch series' sleep tracking feature a try. However, on the Series 11, balancing sleep tracking and charging was a bit of a hassle. After wearing the watch all day, I'd need to charge it once before bed and again after waking up.

The Series 12 is a completely different story, however. Its battery is more than enough to last the entire day and night, so I now only need to charge it once after waking up. The Apple Watch Series 12 also charges noticeably faster, greatly reducing this annoyance. According to Apple, 15 minutes of charging provides up to 12 hours of use.

I suspect the new S11 chip—based on a 2nm design derived from the A20 Pro—is the main reason for the significantly extended battery life. Whatever the reason, not having to worry about battery life for sleep tracking on the Apple Watch Series 12 is a huge relief. Another major advantage of the S11 chip? The Apple Watch Series 12 is noticeably faster, especially when using Siri.

Exclusive Software Features

The Series 12 finally adds an official step counter as a watch face complication, and I love seeing this information in the Smart Stack. Will this feature be rolled out to older Apple Watch models? Most likely, yes. After all, Apple is no stranger to counting steps. The step counting on the Apple Watch Series 12 is indeed more accurate, but given that the relevant data has been around for a while, I feel Apple should have added this complication much sooner. Regardless, it's great that the Series 12 has this feature.

Another excellent new feature is the new Readiness app, which tells you how you're doing today based on your previous night's sleep, your activity level from the day before, and your vital signs. This is similar to WHOOP's recovery score, and I'm certainly thrilled that Apple has added this feature to the Apple Watch. Unfortunately, however, this feature is exclusive to the Series 12, but I understand Apple wouldn't want to calculate this metric using less accurate data.

Conclusion

Overall, the Apple Watch Series 12 is a remarkable upgrade. This is clearly an "S" year update, but if what you care about is practical functional improvements to the Apple Watch rather than just cosmetic changes, I feel this might be one of the most significant yearly upgrades since the Apple Watch Series 4.

Compared to the Series 10 and 11, the bezels are indeed slightly thicker. For users with dark watch face backgrounds, I barely notice it myself—but I hope Apple will make further improvements in this area in the next generation.

One final point worth mentioning is that the Apple Watch Series 12's aluminum models come equipped with Ceramic Shield 2, making it more scratch-resistant than older Apple Watches. I haven't owned it long enough to truly test this, but so far, my Apple Watch still looks brand new.
